title: Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals Reports Fiscal 2026 Third Quarter Results
summary: - Conference Call and Webcast Today, August 4, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. ET PASADENA, Calif. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 4, 2026-- Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARWR) today announced financial results for its fiscal 2026 third quarter ended June 30, 2026.
body_text: - Conference Call and Webcast Today, August 4, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. ET PASADENA, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 4, 2026-- Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARWR) today announced financial results for its fiscal 2026 third quarter ended June 30, 2026. The Company is hosting a conference call today, August 4, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. ET to discuss the results. “The recent period for Arrowhead included transformational events that support continued growth,” said Christopher Anzalone, Ph.D., President and CEO at Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals. “We recently announced topline results from the SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 studies supporting our continued belief that plozasiran is a best-in-class molecule for patients with a spectrum of triglyceride disorders. Based on these promising results, we acquired a priority review voucher (PRV) that potentially accelerates the process of bringing this important new medicine to patients. On the commercial front, REDEMPLO continued to demonstrate growing momentum and penetration with physicians and patients with familial chylomicronemia syndrome. Lastly, we made strong progress across our broad pipeline of RNAi therapeutic candidates at various stages of development, expanding the opportunity to help patients in diverse disease areas.” Key REDEMPLO® Commercial Events U.S. REDEMPLO launch continued to build momentum during the quarter. Key progress included: REDEMPLO prescription volume roughly doubled during the fiscal third quarter. More than 400 unique practitioners have now prescribed REDEMPLO, with the specialty mix led by preventive cardiology and endocrinology. REDEMPLO now has favorable policies in place for the most significant U.S. payers and overall coverage is progressing at a fast trajectory. Announced marketing authorizations of REDEMPLO in two new territories: The European Commission (EC) formally granted marketing authorization for REDEMPLO as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglyceride levels in adult patients with FCS. REDEMPLO is the first and only siRNA medicine authorized by the EC for adults with FCS, diagnosed either by the presence of clinical criteria or genetic testing. The Australian Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) approved REDEMPLO, as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglyceride levels for adult patients with FCS in Australia. Key R&D Events Announced topline results for the global Phase 3 SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 clinical studies of plozasiran in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG). Detailed results will be presented as a HOT LINE Late Breaker at the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Congress on August 30, 2026. SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 successfully met the primary endpoint of triglyceride reduction versus placebo and met all prespecified secondary endpoints in both studies. Deep, durable, and consistent median triglyceride reductions of 79% and 81% from baseline were observed in SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4, respectively. Statistically significant 78% reduction in acute pancreatitis (AP) events versus placebo was observed across the entire sHTG study population, with an unprecedented 100% event reduction in patients with triglycerides above 880 mg/dL and a prior medical history of AP, widely considered to be at the highest risk for AP. Continued and consistent safety and tolerability profile was demonstrated, with no new safety signals and a favorable liver safety profile. Announced that the Company completed enrollment in the global Phase 3 YOSEMITE clinical trial of zodasiran, the Company’s investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapeutic being developed as a potential treatment for homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH), a rare genetic condition that leads to severely elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and early-onset cardiovascular disease. The Company anticipates that YOSEMITE will be completed in mid-2027 and, pending successful clinical results, intends to seek regulatory approval in multiple geographies thereafter. YOSEMITE was initially designed to enroll 60 participants with HoFH; however, strong global patient and physician interest led to an increase in target enrollment to 70 patients. Presented interim results at the European Association for the Study of the Liver Congress (EASL 2026) from a Phase 1/2a clinical trial of ARO-INHBE, the company’s investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapeutic being developed as a potential treatment for obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). The interim data demonstrate that ARO-INHBE treatment led to clinically meaningful reductions in liver fat as a monotherapy and in combination with low-dose tirzepatide, a GLP-1/GIP receptor co-agonist, in adults with obesity. Reported new positive plozasiran clinical data in two oral presentations at the 94th European Atherosclerosis Society (EAS) Congress. The data support plozasiran use in patients with moderate-to-severe renal impairment or moderate hepatic impairment without the need for dose adjustment and suggests that preconception exposure to plozasiran may be associated with sustained lowering of fasting triglyceride levels through the term of a pregnancy. Key Corporate Events Acquired a U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) priority review voucher, which the company intends to use with its upcoming plozasiran sNDA submission, anticipated before the end of 2026, to potentially expand the approved indication to include patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG). A Priority Review designation accelerates FDA’s goal to take action on an application within 6 months, compared to 10 months under standard review. Announced an exclusive worldwide license agreement with Madrigal Pharmaceuticals for ARO-PNPLA3, Arrowhead’s clinical stage RNAi therapeutic designed to reduce liver expression of patatin-like phospholipase domain containing 3 (PNPLA3) as a potential treatment for patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Under the terms of the agreement, Madrigal has made a $25 million upfront payment to Arrowhead. Arrowhead is also eligible to receive development, regulatory, and sales milestone payments of up to $975 million. Arrowhead is further eligible to receive tiered royalties on commercial sales ranging from high-single digits to mid-teens. In a Phase 1 single-ascending dose clinical study, ARO-PNPLA3 achieved encouraging results, including a dose-dependent mean reduction in liver fat of up to 40% in patients homozygous for the I148M mutation, demonstrated no apparent treatment emergent increases in triglycerides or LDL-cholesterol, and had a positive safety and tolerability profile at all doses studied. A replay of the webcast will be available approximately two hours after the conclusion of the call. For analysts that wish to participate in the conference call, please register at https://register-conf.media-server.com/register/BIe3d7a8269de14d348890ebe006a5b6a1 . REDEMPLO is the first and only siRNA treatment approved in these countries to be studied in both clinically diagnosed and genetically confirmed patients living with FCS. REDEMPLO is designed to suppress the production of apolipoprotein C-III (APOC3), a protein produced in the liver that raises triglyceride levels by slowing their breakdown and clearance. By targeting APOC3 with sustained silencing, REDEMPLO delivers significant reductions in triglyceride levels. REDEMPLO is self-administered via subcutaneous injection once every three months. REDEMPLO has been granted Orphan Medicinal Product Designation by the EMA for the treatment of patients with FCS, and Breakthrough Therapy Designation, Fast Track Designation, and Orphan Drug Designation by the U.S. FDA for the treatment of patients with FCS and was also granted Breakthrough Therapy designation by the U.S. FDA in severe hypertriglyceridemia. Sanofi acquired the rights to develop and commercialize REDEMPLO in Greater China, with Arrowhead retaining rights to REDEMPLO in all geographies, outside of Greater China. For more information about REDEMPLO, visit Our Medicines . The company has built a broad portfolio of clinical and commercial RNAi therapeutics through its industry-leading targeted RNAi molecule (TRiM™) platform, which can precisely silence genes in a wide range of cell types, including liver, lung, muscle, adipose, and central nervous system tissue. At Arrowhead, we rapidly advance potential best- and first-in-class RNAi treatments for diseases with significant unmet medical need, because every day matters to the patients we serve. title: Data Rooms for AI Agents: What to Let an Agent Do, and What Never to Let It Do
summary: An AI agent can fill a data room today. The unsolved half is permission: which actions to allow, and how to scope a key so it cannot do the rest.
body_text: An AI agent data room is a data room an agent can drive with a key and a command instead of a browser: it reads which documents are still missing, finds them, uploads each one against the item it satisfies, and re-reads the list to confirm the gap closed. That access exists today at several vendors, so the interesting question is no longer whether an agent can operate a room. It is which actions an agent should be permitted to take at all, and how the credential is scoped so it cannot take the others. Start with that split, because it is the entire design. Action in a live deal room Give it to an agent? Why Read the document list and folder tree Yes Read-only and verifiable Read the readiness checklist and its gaps Yes The gap list is the agent's work order Upload a document Yes Additive; a wrong file is visible and removable Attach a document to a checklist item Yes Makes the agent's work checkable item by item Create and name folders Yes Reversible in seconds Download document contents Only with a key minted for it Bytes leaving the room is a separate decision Delete a document or folder Only with a human confirming Destructive, and failure is silent Grant or revoke a person's access Never Confidentiality boundary Send an invitation or change a link's terms Never Discloses documents to a human being Mark a diligence item complete or not applicable Never A judgment a counterparty relies on The line has nothing to do with how capable the model is. It tracks which actions are additive and reversible, which are destructive, and which disclose confidential material or put a decision on the record. An agent that files a document in the wrong folder costs someone two minutes. An agent that emails a share link to the wrong address ends a deal. Why the permission line falls where it does Three categories, and they behave differently under failure. Additive and reversible. Uploading, creating folders, attaching a document to a checklist item, reading an inventory. When the agent is wrong, the room holds an extra file in the wrong place. A human sees it, moves it, and nothing left the building. This is where an agent earns its keep, and it is the most tedious part of standing up a room. Destructive. Deleting a document or a folder. The failure mode is silent, and recovery depends entirely on what the product does with a deletion. Ask every vendor the same question: when a folder is deleted, what happens to the documents inside it? In our data room, deleting a folder moves its documents to Unsorted and never deletes them, and the client asks for confirmation unless you pass a flag saying you know what you are doing. That design predates agents, but it is the reason an agent can hold a delete permission without it being reckless. Disclosive or on the record. Granting access, sending an invitation, changing what a share link permits, or marking a diligence item complete. Each one either puts confidential documents in front of a human being or records a judgment the other side will rely on. These are not agent actions at any capability level, and the last section explains why that is structural rather than a limitation waiting to be lifted. Which data rooms can an agent actually reach today? More than the "nobody has built this" framing suggests. Everything below was read on August 1, 2026. Datasite states on its diligence product page that you can connect Claude, ChatGPT, or Microsoft Copilot through MCP, with data staying inside Diligence. Its public AI organization also publishes an agent skills repository describing eight coordinated skills for sell-side deal teams, including index setup and matching an information request list against room content, and its stated requirements name Claude Code as a supported host. Ideals promotes an MCP connector in the top banner of its homepage, connecting Claude, Copilot, and ChatGPT to the data room. On its pricing page, that connector and an API integration add-on sit under the Enterprise tier, which is worth noting: at some vendors, agent reach is a pricing decision rather than a product one. DealRoom advertises an MCP integration on its pricing page for connecting deal data to any MCP-compatible AI. Papermark, a data room vendor, publishes an MCP server on npm from its own scope and its own repository, declaring a runnable executable, last published on July 27, 2026. Two observations about the shape of that race. First, MCP and a command line client are different access surfaces, and no established deal VDR publishes a command line client on npm, checked August 1, 2026; the vendor-by-vendor check is in our piece on the data room command line client . Do not read that as a moat. Box publishes an official command line interface for the Box API on npm under its own maintainer accounts, last published June 1, 2026, and Box sells a virtual data room for managing mergers on its own site. Read "data room vendor" at its plain meaning and the gap closes. Second, look at who published the package. A CLI named papermark-cli exists on npm and describes itself as an agent-first CLI for data room workflows, but an individual publishes it from a personal repository, not the vendor. That distinction matters more for an agent than for a person: a community wrapper holds your credential, tracks the vendor's API on its own schedule, and answers to nobody when it breaks mid-process. How do you scope a credential so an agent cannot touch the wrong room? This is where a design either exists or does not, and it is the question I would put first in any vendor call. In our data room, an agent needs one environment variable and nothing else. Set MAGE_API_KEY and skip the login step entirely; the client discovers which room the key belongs to on first use. That is the documented path for agents and for continuous integration, and the reason it matters is negative rather than positive: the agent never holds a browser session, never drives a UI, and never runs as you. What a room-scoped key can and cannot do: It acts in its own room only. It cannot reach another room in your organization. It carries the permission set chosen when it was minted, and those permissions are immutable. Widening a key means minting a new one, which is a deliberate human act with its own record. It cannot delete the room. It cannot change room settings, people, or sharing without a Manage room permission that is not granted by default. It cannot fetch document contents without a Download permission. Reading the document list and reading the bytes are two different grants. Revoking it under Settings, API keys kills it everywhere instantly. The secret itself is returned exactly once, at creation. What the room records is: the room binding, who minted it, a snapshot of its permissions, and the audit trail. On a developer's machine, the client keeps its credential in a config file readable only by that user. The practical version is short. Mint the narrowest key the task needs, hand it to the agent, revoke it when the task is done. A browser login cannot offer that, because it carries every permission you hold in every room you can see, for as long as the session lives. Does agent access break the audit trail, or improve it? It improves it, and this is the claim I expect to argue about. Consider the honest baseline in a live process. An associate is signed into an account several people know the password to. A session is open on a laptop in a conference room. Views and downloads land on the room's log attributed to whoever's session it was, which is frequently not the person who did the work. Nobody calls that an audit failure because it is what everyone has always done. A scoped key inverts it. The credential is minted for one purpose, named for the machine it lives on, listed in the room's settings with its permission set and the person who created it, and revocable in one click. Every file it downloads lands on the room's access audit trail like any other. When something goes wrong, three questions have answers a shared login cannot produce: what was this credential allowed to do, what did it actually do, and who authorized it. The serious objection is not that agents are unaccountable. It is that they act quickly and at volume, so a mistake propagates before anyone notices. That is real, and its answer is the same mechanism: narrow the permission set, keep revocation one click away. Both are properties of the credential, not of the model. What the loop actually looks like Four steps, and the third is the only one that is not obvious. mage readiness --json returns the room's checklist as machine-readable items. Each carries an id, a label, a status of missing, partial, or present, and a hint describing what the item should contain. The agent finds those documents with its own tools, wherever they live. mage upload <file> --for-item <itemId> uploads the file and attaches it to that checklist item in one call. mage readiness --json again, to confirm the item closed. Repeat until nothing required is missing. Every command accepts --json and emits machine-readable output on stdout. That is the boring detail the whole loop rests on. A tool an agent has to screen-scrape is a tool an agent cannot verify, and an agent that cannot verify its own work is just a faster way to produce a mess. Step three changes the character of the work. Uploading a file is a blind action; uploading it against the item it satisfies is a claim that can be checked. When the agent finishes, the room's own checklist is the report card, in the same view a human would have read anyway. The product ships the prompt, so nobody has to write one. The key-based version reads: Fill my Mage data room. With MAGE_API_KEY="<key>" , run npx @magelegal/cli readiness --json to see which checklist items are missing, find those documents in my files or other services, and upload each one with npx @magelegal/cli upload <file> --for-item <itemId> until nothing required is missing. A realistic task on top of that: pull last year's tax return from our accounting system and satisfy the missing tax items in the readiness checklist. The client is @magelegal/cli , MIT licensed, public source, Node.js 20 or newer, and runnable with npx without installing anything. The command reference, flags, and the human-at-a-terminal walkthrough live in the Mage data room CLI . One boundary worth stating plainly: this client drives the data room only. Mage's diligence platform has no command line surface, and I would rather say that here than have you discover it after a purchase. Why does a browser-only room become the bottleneck? Because everything on either side of it is already scriptable. The documents originate in systems with APIs. Cap tables, financial statements, payroll exports, signed agreements, board consents: they live in software an agent can already reach. Downstream, review is software too. What the room does to a document once it lands, meaning typing, filing, numbering, and gap-checking, is covered in AI data rooms , and the handoff from a full room into diligence is covered in from data room to diligence workflow . The room in the middle is the only step that has traditionally required a person, a mouse, and an afternoon. When the two steps around it are automated, the manual one stops being a step and starts being a queue. There is a worse version of solving this, which is pointing a browser-driving agent at the room's UI. It works in a demo. It is brittle against any interface change, it is slow, and above all it runs inside a human's full session, which puts you back at every permission that person holds in every room. UI automation is not agent access. It is a person's credential with a robot's hands. What must a human still sign off on, and why is that permanent? Because models produce confident wrong answers, and in diligence a confident wrong answer is worse than no answer. A tool that says nothing is missing, and is wrong, does not merely fail to help. It removes the item from the reviewer's attention. That asymmetry does not go away with a better model, so the design has to absorb it. Three things stay human in our room by construction rather than by policy. Who gets access. Invitations mint one personalized link per recipient and email it to them, and every view on that link is attributable to the person it was issued to. That is a decision about who sees confidential material, which means it belongs to a person who can be asked why. What a link permits. Whether it requires an NDA, whether it carries a watermark, whether it allows download, whether printing is allowed separately from download, and when it expires. These are per-link settings a human chooses. On the watermark specifically: per-viewer stamping puts the viewer's identity and the date on every page, and it is a deterrent, not an access control. Anyone selling watermarking as leak prevention is selling you something. Telling other people the room changed. Reading the readiness checklist and curating individual items accept a room-scoped key, which is what lets an agent attach what it uploads. Triggering a recompute and notifying people are gated to a signed-in human. The split is deliberate: an agent may do the work, and a person decides when the work is announced. The same reasoning is why the table at the top says an agent should attach documents to an item but should not be the one declaring the item done, even where the credential would permit it. That is not a temporary boundary awaiting a smarter model. It is the same boundary that governs a first-year associate, drawn in software instead of in a supervision policy. Where to start Run the loop against a real room and see whether it holds up. Our data room is free for a limited time and self-serve, so you can hand a key to your own agent this afternoon without talking to anybody: it is at the Mage Data Room page . Mage is SOC 2 Type II certified, which covers the security controls and says nothing about whether your agent filed a document correctly, which is exactly the point of keeping the checklist as the report card. The rest of our writing on how these rooms should work sits in the data rooms topic hub .

title: How to Get an Internship at PwC 2026-2027
summary: The complete guide to PwC internships: compare programs, Summer 2027 internship openings, and interview prep.
body_text: To get a PwC internship, choose the student path, season, service line, and office before you apply. Start and Advance serve different college stages, Winter requires full-time busy-season availability, and the interview format changes between Audit, Tax, Digital Assurance and Transparency, and Advisory. What You Should Know About PwC Internships Start and Advance are not interchangeable. Start serves earlier college students and can lead to an Advance offer; Advance typically takes place about one year before graduation. The office can close before the broader program. PwC recruits for many roles on a rolling basis by location, so a listed office may disappear as offers are accepted. The interview depends on the service line. Audit, Tax, and DAT use two behavioral interviews, while most Advisory roles require a case interview. PwC Internships at a Glance Question Verified US answer What is open now? PwC's official US site references Summer 2027 searches, but no verified US internship was active in Simplify on August 2, 2026. What are the main paths? Start for earlier college students and Advance for students approaching graduation, plus separate Summer and Winter schedules. How long is the work week? PwC says internships are full time and require at least 40 hours each week. When do roles close? Most roles recruit on a rolling basis by office and can close as positions fill. Is an assessment required? Most entry-level applications are incomplete until the emailed assessment is submitted. How do interviews differ? Audit, Tax, and DAT use two behavioral interviews; most Advisory roles include a case interview. 🔎 No verified US internship was active in Simplify on August 2, 2026. The only US match in PwC's globally tagged inventory was a full-time Tax JD Associate role. This guide omits the job card and sends applicants to PwC's official entry-level search for current availability. Are PwC Summer 2027 Internships Open? PwC's official US recruiting FAQ tells candidates to search its entry-level board for phrases such as "summer 2027." Its student pages also reference 2027 Start and client-service pathways. That confirms active 2027 recruiting infrastructure, but it does not mean every service line or office is currently accepting applications. Use the exact official result as the open-or-closed authority. PwC says most opportunities recruit on a rolling basis. A location can close as offers are accepted, even while the broader program still appears on the careers site. Summer internships generally run from June through mid-August. Winter internships run from January through March or April and require at least 40 hours each week. The company advises students not to take classes during a Winter term. For broader recruiting context, use Simplify's Summer 2027 internship timeline , then return to PwC's official search for the service line and office you want. A historical opening month cannot replace the live posting. What Is the Difference Between PwC Start and Advance? Path Who it serves When it happens Important distinction Career Preview Freshmen in four-year programs or sophomores in five-year programs who meet program criteria Three-day experience Exploration program, not an internship Start Internship Sophomores in four-year programs, juniors in five-year programs, and eligible associate-degree transfers Summer Can lead to an Advance offer in the same career area Advance Internship Usually students one year before graduation Summer or Winter Client work and the main internship experience Winter Internship Students who can work full time during busy season January-March or April PwC advises against taking classes during the term Start is PwC's earlier-college internship. The official eligibility tool names sophomores in four-year bachelor's programs, juniors in five-year programs, and eligible associate-degree students transferring to a four-year institution. A Start offer in many career areas can include an Advance offer for the following summer. Follow the exact offer because Product and Technology may differ. Advance typically takes place about one year before graduation and includes training, client assignments, coaching, and networking. PwC says more than 90% of its interns receive full-time offers. That is a return-offer outcome, not an internship acceptance rate. Career Preview and Destination CPA are development experiences, not internships. 📅 Winter means full time. PwC's Winter internships run during Audit and Tax busy season. They are not part-time placements to stack beside a normal class schedule. What Internships Does PwC Offer? PwC separates student work by service line. Choose the client problem and evidence type before choosing a familiar office or title. The four families below cover the main US internship paths without treating every global PwC member firm as one recruiting system. Audit and Digital Assurance Audit interns support financial statement work, testing, documentation, and evidence review. Digital Assurance and Transparency, often shortened to DAT, examines controls, transactions, business processes, and technology risks across cloud, AI, and other systems. Both paths require accuracy and professional skepticism, but DAT adds more technology-control depth. Best proof: an audit, reconciliation, control test, or data review where you found an issue and supported the conclusion. Tax Tax internships can involve compliance, research, planning, transfer pricing, deals, data, and process automation. Some teams expect a CPA-oriented accounting path; others combine tax knowledge with analytics or software. Read the education language carefully instead of assuming every Tax role has the same degree requirement. Best proof: research or analysis that connects a rule, source, calculation, review step, and defensible recommendation. Advisory Advisory teams work on strategy, transactions, operations, risk, cybersecurity, technology transformation, and other client problems. The work and recruiting process differ by practice, which is why PwC does not publish one universal Advisory interview. Most Advisory positions include a case interview. Best proof: a structured recommendation that defines the client problem, tests assumptions, weighs tradeoffs, and shows how the analysis changed an outcome. Technology and Engineering Technology work appears inside DAT, Tax technology, Advisory, cloud and data teams, internal products, and engineering programs. Candidates may build automation, analyze systems, test controls, work with data, or support technical transformation. The business setting matters as much as the tool list. Best proof: a deployed system or automation with architecture, testing, reliability, user impact, and a clear account of your own contribution. Audit and Digital Assurance The work and candidate fit. Audit interns can support financial statement testing, evidence review, documentation, and client requests. DAT interns focus more directly on controls, transactions, technology processes, and readiness work. Accounting students may fit traditional Audit, while information systems, analytics, or technology-risk students may find DAT more natural. The August 2 inventory check found no qualifying US internship, so the next official requisition must supply the degree, CPA-credit, location, work-authorization, and compensation terms. What to show and prepare. Use a reconciliation, accounting project, control review, data-quality check, or systems audit. Explain the assertion or risk, evidence gathered, test performed, exception found, and conclusion. PwC says Audit and DAT candidates complete two behavioral interviews back to back in a live virtual format. Prepare examples around accuracy, handling incomplete evidence, raising a concern, learning a client process, and working through a deadline. Students building this evidence can use Simplify's accounting internship guide . Tax The work and candidate fit. PwC Tax covers compliance, research, structuring, transactions, transfer pricing, and technology-enabled work. Some teams are closely tied to accounting and CPA eligibility. Tax Technology and Automation can favor candidates who combine business knowledge with data, process, or software skills. Do not assume the same academic requirements across every Tax posting. No verified current US internship supplied a pay band for this draft, and the full-time Tax JD Associate that appeared in the internship index was excluded from the module. What to show and prepare. Prepare one example where a rule affected a calculation or recommendation. Show the authority or data source, your method, review steps, uncertainty, and conclusion. For technology-oriented Tax work, add the process you automated and how you checked accuracy. PwC says Tax candidates use the same two-interview behavioral format as Audit and DAT. Expect questions about deadlines, detailed work, client communication, and how you respond when an answer needs more research rather than a quick guess. Advisory The work and candidate fit. Advisory spans strategy, transactions, operations, risk, cybersecurity, cloud, data, and transformation. That breadth makes practice selection important. A transaction candidate should bring different evidence from a cyber, supply-chain, or cloud candidate. Start with the problem the selected practice solves, then connect coursework and projects to its deliverables. PwC's current Simplify inventory contained no qualifying US Advisory internship on August 2, so availability and requirements must be checked on the official US board. What to show and prepare. Build a short case from your own experience: define the problem, identify the decision maker, structure the analysis, compare options, and state what happened. PwC says most Advisory roles require a case interview, but the invitation explains the process for the selected practice. Practice explaining calculations and recommendations aloud, asking clarifying questions, and separating facts from assumptions. Candidates should prepare commercial judgment for the exact team rather than memorizing one generic consulting framework. Technology and Engineering The work and candidate fit. PwC uses technology inside Audit, DAT, Tax, and Advisory as well as in dedicated cloud, data, automation, product, and engineering teams. Intern work can include coding, process automation, data analysis, system testing, controls, or technical delivery for clients. A computer science student should identify whether the role is software building, technology consulting, or assurance before tailoring the resume. No active US role was available for a current language, degree, location, or compensation comparison. What to show and prepare. Use a project with users, tests, and a measurable operating result. Be ready to diagram the system, explain data flow, justify tradeoffs, trace a defect, and discuss reliability or security. If the role sits in Advisory, prepare for a case that uses technical information to reach a business recommendation. If it sits in DAT, prepare to reason about controls and evidence. Simplify's current internship listings can help compare the requirements used in current technical postings. What Is the PwC Internship Schedule Like? PwC internships require at least 40 hours each week. Summer generally runs from June through mid-August. Winter runs from January through March or April during Audit and Tax busy season, so students should not plan a normal class schedule alongside it. The experience depends on the office and service line. Confirm travel, hybrid expectations, overtime, school conflicts, and the exact end date before accepting. How Hard Is It to Get a PwC Internship? PwC does not publish a verified US internship acceptance rate. Visible filters include student stage, graduation timing, service-line fit, office availability, requisition requirements, and assessment completion. An office can close while the broader program remains visible. PwC says more than 90% of its interns receive full-time offers. That describes conversion after the program, not admission. PwC publishes no universal US intern wage, so use the exact requisition or offer. How Do I Apply for a PwC Internship? Choose Start or Advance. Use class year and graduation timing first. Career Preview is exploratory, not an internship application. Choose Summer or Winter. Winter requires full-time weekday availability during busy season; Summer generally runs June through mid-August. Choose one service line and office. Audit, DAT, Tax, Advisory, and technology roles use different evidence, and rolling locations can close separately. Apply on PwC's entry-level site. PwC says not to submit the internship resume through a university career site. Upload a current PDF and follow the exact office instructions. Complete the assessment promptly. For most entry-level roles, the application is incomplete until the assessment emailed after submission is finished. Track each application and interview path. Save the season, office, service line, graduation window, resume version, assessment date, and next step. At PwC, one application can contain several deadlines. Track the program, service line, office, season, graduation window, resume PDF, assessment, and interview stage before a rolling location closes. Track your PwC applications → How Should I Prepare for a PwC Internship Interview? PwC publishes a clear service-line split. Audit, Tax, and DAT candidates complete two live virtual behavioral interviews back to back. Most Advisory positions require a case interview, with details supplied in the invitation. PwC also says candidates may not use generative AI during the assessment or interview process. For Audit, DAT, and Tax, prepare evidence stories. Use examples about accuracy, deadlines, unclear information, client or team communication, and a time you corrected your own work. For Advisory, practice a spoken case. Clarify the objective, structure the problem, state assumptions, work through evidence, and make a concise recommendation. Use the PwC Professional framework carefully. Connect each answer to a real action and result instead of repeating leadership language from the careers page. Know every line of the resume. Review the calculation, source, control, code, or analysis behind each claim and keep confidential client or school data out of shared materials. PwC Internship FAQ Is it hard to get a PwC internship? PwC does not publish a verified acceptance rate. Applicants must match the program stage, graduation window, service line, and office, then finish the required assessment before rolling locations close. Do PwC interns get paid? PwC does not publish one universal US intern wage on its program pages. Use the employer-posted compensation on the exact requisition or offer rather than a third-party average. When do PwC internship applications open? PwC posts Summer and Winter roles separately and recruits for many openings on a rolling basis. Its official search supports Summer 2027 queries, but dates and availability differ by office and service line. What is the easiest way to get a PwC internship? There is no verified easy service line. Choose the program and office whose requirements you meet, then use evidence suited to Audit, Tax, Advisory, DAT, or technology work. What is the difference between PwC Start and Advance? Start serves earlier college students and can lead to an Advance offer for the following summer. Advance usually takes place about one year before graduation and includes client work. Does the PwC internship application require an assessment? Most PwC entry-level roles require an assessment. PwC says the application is incomplete until that assessment is submitted, although listed role categories may be exempt. title: What Are the Dimensions of Popular Storage Unit Sizes in Minneapolis?
summary: Popular storage unit sizes in Minneapolis include 5×5, 7×10, 5×15, 10×10, 10×15, 10×20, 10×25, and 10×30. body_text: Popular storage unit sizes in Minneapolis include 5×5, 7×10, 5×15, 10×10, 10×15, 10×20, 10×25, and 10×30 . These sizes range from about 25 square feet of floor space for 5×5 units to about 300 square feet for a 10×30 unit. For people living in Minneapolis, the size of the storage unit you need usually depends on your location and purpose. If you live in an apartment in areas like Downtown Minneapolis or Uptown, you may only need a small storage unit, such as a 5×5 or 5×10, for extra items. However, if you are moving, renovating your home, or downsizing, you might require a larger unit, such as a 10×15, 10×20, or even bigger. Popular Storage Unit Sizes in Minneapolis Unit Size Floor Space Comparable Size Common Uses 5×5 25 sq. ft. Small Walk-In Closet Small business inventory, seasonal items, small furniture 5×10 50 sq. ft. Small Shed Small bedroom or apartment belongings 5×15 75 sq. ft. Large Utility Room Furniture, seasonal sports equipment, appliances, mattress and bed frame 10×10 100 sq. ft. Slightly smaller than an SUV Living room furniture, Bicycles, Washer, Dryer 10×15 150 sq. ft. One Car garage Home office furniture, primary bedroom, season tools 10×20 200 sq. ft. Small Studio Apartment Patio furniture, Dressers, two or three sofas, refrigerator 10×25 250 sq. ft. Large Storage Shed Contents of a three- to four-bedroom home Storage unit dimensions are generally expressed as width by length . Exact dimensions and ceiling heights can vary by Minneapolis facility and individual unit. What Are the Dimensions of a 5×5 Storage Unit in Minneapolis? A 5×5 storage unit is approximately 5 feet wide by 5 feet long, providing about 25 square feet of floor space . Comparable to a large closet, this compact size can work well for Minneapolis apartment residents who need extra room for: Boxes and storage bins Holiday decorations Seasonal clothing Small furniture Sporting equipment Small business inventory For someone living in an apartment or condo in areas such as North Loop, Uptown, or Linden Hills, a 5×5 unit can provide additional storage without renting significantly more space than needed. What Are the Dimensions of a 5×10 Storage Unit in Minneapolis? A 5×10 storage unit is roughly 5 feet wide by 10 feet long, offering around 50 square feet of floor space . Comparable to the size of a walk-in closet, a 5×10 unit can accommodate: Bedroom furniture A mattress and bed frame Boxes and storage bins Small appliances Bikes Seasonal belongings This size is particularly beneficial for Minneapolis renters who are transitioning between apartments or require extra space for bedroom contents. What Are the Dimensions of a 5×15 Storage Unit in Minneapolis? A 5×15 storage unit measures approximately 5 feet wide by 15 feet long, providing about 75 square feet of floor space . The longer layout offers additional room for furniture and other bulky belongings, such as: Living room sofas and chairs Mattresses and bed frames Kitchen appliances Dressers and wardrobes Boxes and household items A 5×15 unit is an ideal choice for Minneapolis residents who have exceeded the capacity of a smaller unit and do not require the full 100 square feet of a 10×10 unit. What Are the Dimensions of a 10×10 Storage Unit in Minneapolis? A 10×10 storage unit measures approximately 10 feet wide by 10 feet long and provides about 100 square feet of floor space . Its footprint is roughly half the size of a one-car garage, providing room for items such as: Living room furniture Complete bedroom sets Mattresses Dining furniture Laundry and kitchen appliances Boxes and storage containers Whether you’re transitioning between student housing, apartments, or houses in Minneapolis, or just need some extra room to stash belongings from a few rooms, a 10×10 unit provides just the right amount of space without having to oversize. What Are the Dimensions of a 10×15 Storage Unit in Minneapolis? A 10×15 storage unit measures approximately 10 feet wide by 15 feet long, providing about 150 square feet of floor space . This size may accommodate furniture and belongings from several rooms, including: Living room furniture Bedroom sets Household appliances Dining room table and chairs Mattresses Storage boxes A 10×15 unit is especially handy during a move or home renovation when you need more space than a 10×10 can offer. What Are the Dimensions of a 10×20 Storage Unit in Minneapolis? A 10×20 storage unit measures approximately 10 feet wide by 20 feet long and provides about 200 square feet of floor space . This is approximately equivalent to a one-car garage . Depending on your belongings’ size and quantity, a 10×20 unit can comfortably hold the contents of a three-bedroom Minneapolis home, including furnishings, appliances, mattresses, and boxes. This size is particularly advantageous during substantial moves, extensive renovations, or transitions between homes. What Are the Dimensions of a 10×25 Storage Unit in Minneapolis? A 10×25 storage unit measures approximately 10 feet wide by 25 feet long, providing about 250 square feet of floor space . A 10×25 storage unit offers plenty of space, perfect for fitting everything from a three- to four-bedroom home, depending on how much stuff you have. It’s got room for those big pieces of furniture, essential appliances, complete bedroom sets, dining room tables, various boxes, and more household items. If you’re in Minneapolis and you’re making a big move or need to store most of your home’s contents during a renovation, the extra five feet of length this unit provides compared to a 10×20 can really come in handy, giving you that additional space you need! What Are the Dimensions of a 10×30 Storage Unit in Minneapolis? A 10×30 storage unit measures approximately 10 feet wide by 30 feet long and provides about 300 square feet of floor space . A 10×30 storage unit is one of the largest sizes you can find, making it perfect for holding the contents of a four- to five-bedroom home, depending on how much you have and the size of your items. It’s an ideal option for big moves around Minneapolis, extensive renovations, or when you need to securely store furniture, appliances, boxes, and various other belongings all in one place. What Should Minneapolis Residents Consider When Choosing a Storage Unit Size? In addition to dimensions, Minneapolis residents should consider what they’re storing, how long they plan to store it, and how often they’ll need access . First, grab a tape measure and jot down the sizes of your bigger items like sofas, mattresses, dining tables, and any appliances or furniture pieces. Then, think about how many boxes or storage bins you’ll need to tuck in around them. Remember, Minneapolis weather can have its mood swings! If you’ve got items that don’t like extreme temperatures or humidity, you might want to think about getting a climate-controlled storage unit. And don’t forget about convenience—pick a storage location near your home, apartment, workplace, or along your usual routes. It’ll make popping in and out with your stuff a whole lot easier! What Size Storage Unit Do I Need in Minneapolis? As a general guide: 5×5: Good for boxes, seasonal belongings, and small furniture. 5×10: Useful for a bedroom’s contents or additional apartment storage. 5×15: Provides more room for furniture, appliances, and boxes. 10×10: Can accommodate furniture and belongings from multiple rooms. 10×15: Useful for larger moves and multi-room storage. 10×20: About the footprint of a one-car garage and may hold the contents of a three-bedroom home. 10×25: May accommodate belongings from a three- to four-bedroom home. 10×30: Provides ample space for belongings from a four- to five-bedroom home. These are general estimates. The amount of space you need will depend on the size, number, and arrangement of your belongings. Frequently Asked Questions About Storage Unit Sizes in Minneapolis What is the most common storage unit size in Minneapolis? Minneapolis storage facilities offer a range of sizes, commonly including 5×5, 5×10, 10×10, 10×15, 10×20, and other configurations. Availability varies by facility. How big is a 10×10 storage unit in Minneapolis? A 10×10 storage unit provides approximately 100 square feet of floor space . Its footprint is roughly half the size of a one-car garage, offering space for furniture, appliances, boxes, and belongings from multiple rooms. What size storage unit do I need for a Minneapolis apartment? If you just have a few extra items from your apartment, a 5×5 might do the trick. For more room to store furniture and boxes, consider a 5×10 or 5×15 . If you’re looking to store things from multiple rooms, a 10×10 could be a better fit. Ultimately, the best size boils down to how much you have and the size of each item. What size storage unit do I need for a one-bedroom Minneapolis home? A 5×10 or 5×15 storage unit is just the right size for packing up everything from a cozy one-bedroom home or apartment in Minneapolis. You can fit your bedroom furniture, small appliances, boxes, and other household goodies. Choosing the perfect size depends on how much stuff you’ve got and their sizes—so think about your stash and pick what works best for you! What size storage unit do I need for a two-bedroom Minneapolis home? A 10×10 or 10×15 storage unit can fit everything from a two-bedroom home or apartment in Minneapolis, including furniture from the bedrooms and living room, appliances, mattresses, and boxes. If you have bulkier furniture or just need a little more space, opting for a 10×15 might be the way to go. What size storage unit do I need for a three-bedroom Minneapolis home? A 10×20 storage unit may accommodate the contents of a three-bedroom home, depending on the amount and size of the furniture, appliances, boxes, and other belongings being stored. Should I consider climate-controlled storage in Minneapolis? If your items don’t like temperature extremes, you might want to think about climate-controlled storage. Given that Minneapolis can swing from really hot to really cold, it’s a good idea to consider what you’re storing and for how long when choosing the right storage options for you.
